newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan 97/98 crude steel output seen below 99 mln T.
newsitem.headline: Japan 97/98 crude steel output seen below 99 mln T.

text.p: Japan Iron and Steel Federation said on Monday it expects Japan's total crude steel output will be about 98 million tonnes in the 1997/98 business year, compared with an estimated 99 million tonnes in the 1996/97 business year.
Japan's actual crude steel output in 1995/96 was 100.02 million tonnes.

The estimated fall in crude steel output in 1997/98 is due to an expected decline in domestic demand as a result of the planned rise in the consumption tax next year, federation chairman Takashi Imai told a news conference.
The federation expected growth in Japan's real gross domestic product (GDP) to be below 1.5 percent in 1997/98, down from estimated growth of 2.5 percent for this fiscal year, he said.

Poorer prospects for GDP growth will be due to several factors, including the planned consumption tax hike, discontinuation of special income tax cuts, and an expected slowdown in public spending growth, he said.
